articles.title: Barack Obama awarded honorary degree from Queens University Belfast
articles.summary: Receiving his doctorate, the 44th US president praised Northern Ireland's progress and challenged the next generation to continue building a peaceful and inclusive future.
articles.body:
Former US President Barack Obama has been awarded an honorary degree from Queen's University Belfast (QUB).

Receiving his doctorate, the 44th US president praised Northern Ireland's progress and challenged the next generation to continue building a peaceful and inclusive future.

The Good Friday Agreement peace agreement "is still a shining example of what can happen when people put aside old wounds and choose peace," he told university staff and students.

During his visit to Northern Ireland, Obama was due to address an audience of paying fans in Belfast's O2 Arena on Tuesday night.

Accepting the honorary doctorate during a special ceremony at QUB, Obama made a speech that touched on a number of subjects including the peace process and the role young people can play in shaping Northern Ireland's future.

Obama said that, while peace had transformed opportunities across Northern Ireland, its benefits must continue to be shared by all.

Comparing Northern Ireland now to the place he encountered on a visit back in 2013 , he said young people today faced significant challenges but also had reasons to remain hopeful.

"But," he added, "as we have seen in many countries, including in my home country the United States, peace and democracy are not inevitable.

"They have to be chosen, again and again."

During the ceremony, Obama heard from Emma McAllister, a first-year Law with Politics student from north Belfast.

McAllister first engaged with Queen's through a cross-community programme that helped young people from the Ardoyne and Shankill areas to access leadership and educational opportunities.

After listening to McAllister, Obama said: "That's what peace makes possible. And it's what Queen's and the supporters in this room are helping to make real."

In his closing remarks, Obama set out a challenge for students.

"And that is to keep showing the way," he said.

Queen's President and Vice-Chancellor Professor Sir Ian Greer congratulated Obama.

"We are privileged to welcome President Obama to Queen's.

"His commitment to peace, dialogue and public service has left a lasting impact around the world, and particularly here in Northern Ireland."

According to the university, honorary degrees are awarded to those who have achieved distinction or given significant service in one or more of a number of broad constituencies.

This includes business and commerce, the arts, education, medicine, and more.

In 2025, former Manchester United footballer Gary Neville received a QUB honorary degree for his contribution to sport, business, education and philanthropy .

Other notable recipients include boxer Carl Frampton, poet Seamus Heaney, former Irish President Mary McAleese and playwright Brian Friel.

articles.title: Iranian chess grandmaster Mitra Hejazipour: 'The regime can no longer stop this movement'
articles.summary: Mitra Hejazipour: "Mehsa Amini's death was the beginning of the end of this regime. We know that during these years, many people have been killed and impriso...
articles.body:
Iranian chess grandmaster Mitra Hejazipour made headlines in 2020 when she was expelled from the Iranian women's national chess team for refusing to wear the mandatory hijab.

She now lives in Paris and recently became the French women's champion in the lightning blitz competition. She has been a French citizen for a few months and will probably play in the French women's national team in the future. Currently, Hejazipour works for an engineering company in Paris, having studied software engineering in France.

We met up with Hejazipour in Paris to talk about her decision to abandon the mandatory hijab and how Vida Mowahed - the young girl who, five years ago, decided to hang her scarf on a stick near the Revolution Square in Tehran - has impacted her personal life.

Can you tell us about your first encounter with the mandatory hijab?

Mitra Hejazipour: Since I grew up in a religious and traditional family, accepting hijab was a normal thing for me. But the first time I was told that you must wear this mask, I did not like it and felt bad. When we left the country and travelled to other countries, I saw that female athletes sometimes fell behind because of the mandatory hijab and had to work harder to make up for the lost points. Of course, in chess, the hijab is less of an intervention, but as soon as they impose the hijab on you and keep repeating it, it gets on your nerves.

Mandatory hijab is a double pressure, especially when you don't believe in something from the bottom of your heart and you think you have to accept what you don't accept.

I also remember that I was nine years old and I was second in the world under 10 girls chess tournament. A German chess-playing boy of my age wanted to shake my hand to congratulate me, but my manager told me that it was not right."

Your trips were often monitored by security forces. Can you tell us about those experiences?

Surveillance was everywhere, they were trained to be with us and monitor everything. They kept warning us. I remember my first foreign trip with the youth team, when the security forces checked that we ate halal food and that we wore loose-fitting clothes. They kept reminding me to wear hijab. We could not even leave the hotel without their permission. Everywhere you turned, they were present and all our behaviour was monitored.

Tell us about your decision to attend the Moscow chess tournament without the mandatory hijab?

In December 2019, I participated in the Moscow competition without a hijab. Of course, before that I also wrote a text on Instagram and supported the women of Elkhebal Street. When the women of the revolution took off the headscarf, many people criticized them. This made me angry and I wanted to support them. But they called me and my family on behalf of the federation and threatened me."

They told me to delete this post quickly. But I had made my decision and I was angry and I didn't answer the phones. My mother was called and she told me crying that they might arrest me. They were very scared. That's why I had to take that post down.

How did you come to the decision to appear in the Moscow chess tournament in 2019 without a hijab?

At that time, I was playing in a club in France and I went to Moscow directly from France. Since the beginning of the competition, I used to travel everywhere without hijab. Probably the teammates were in contact with the federation and the story had reached their ears.

First, they called very simply and said that you should wear hijab and if you don't, they may boycott the federation. The head of the federation sent me a message saying that you must observe your hijab. He said, "It's very important for us, otherwise we'll throw you out of the tournament and you won't be able to play anymore." Threats like that. But I had made my decision and I wanted to support Vida Mowahed and the women of Elkhebal Street, and deal with the issue of compulsory hijab.

After I played without a hijab, the head of the federation made a statement and said that I was kicked out of the national team and that I will not be able to play for the rest of my life.

Did you inform your family at the time that you weren't going to appear with a hijab?

No, this was a personal decision. As I said, I had not talked to my family. I knew that this decision had consequences, but I wanted not to drown myself in it so that they would not stop my decision.

What was the reaction of other chess players?

I was not supported - at least among chess players. They almost cut off contact with me. I only had a relationship with Sara Khadim al-Sharia and we used to talk to each other. Sara recently decided to participate in the same competitions without hijab and left the country.

What of the stereotypes outside of Iran – how have you experienced your life in France?

Although I carry those stereotypes here too, the experience I had made me get out of these frameworks and think more easily and set higher goals for myself and be sure that I can achieve my goals. Here you think, wanting is being able. Here, women are not considered the second gender. And I can draw important goals for myself and try to achieve them.

What was the impact of Vida Mowahed and the women of Elkhebal Street on changing your approach to the hijab issue?

When Vida Mowahed went to the electrical box near the Revolution Square in Tehran, took off her hijab and tied a scarf on a stick, her decision had a great impact on me. His work was shocking to me. I was asking myself why I didn't protest against this forced pressure all these years and why I was with the crowd and obeyed like everyone else. Her courage was very admirable to me. I was very impressed by Vida Mohed.

The death of this young girl was very sad. It was a great sadness for her family and the people of Iran. But I think the killing of this young girl was a turning point for Iran. Mehsa Amini's death was the beginning of the end of this regime. We know that during these years, many people have been killed and imprisoned by this regime, but this was a turning point for Iran.

How do you see the return of Irshad Patrol (morality police) to the streets?

I have no doubt that this regime does not hesitate to take any measures to suppress people and prevent people from moving. But at the same time, I believe that the change that occurred. When the women of Iran tasted the sense of freedom from the Islamic Republic - this is irreversible. And once you have tasted the feeling of freedom, you will never go back. The regime can no longer stop this movement.

If you could say something to Vida Mowahed, what would it be?

I am very grateful to her. I appreciate her courage. Her action created a spark in the minds of people like me. For many years, we were used to wearing the compulsory hijab. It was not a question for us why we should wear it when we don't believe in it. Vida Mowahed made me understand that we should not lower our heads in front of forceful words. She made us understand that we can protest. Her work was very valuable to me and I will never forget it.

articles.title: Incêndio no Distrito Industrial 2: Justiça suspende atividades | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão liminar atende parcialmente a pedido do MPAM e prevê multa diária de R$ 100 mil em caso de descumprimento. Incêndio começou em 6 de outubro e atingiu mais de 15 mil m².
articles.summary: A Justiça suspendeu licenças ambientais no Distrito Industrial 2 após incêndio de grandes proporções e suspeitas de irregularidades apontadas pelo MPAM em Manaus.
articles.body:
A Justiça do Amazonas determinou a suspensão imediata das licenças ambientais e a paralisação das atividades operacionais e comerciais em uma área atingida por um incêndio de grandes proporções no Distrito Industrial 2 , no início de outubro, em Manaus .

A decisão atende parcialmente a um pedido do Ministério Público do Amazonas (MPAM), que ajuizou uma ação civil pública para apurar possíveis irregularidades ambientais no local.

A liminar foi concedida pela Vara Especializada do Meio Ambiente da Comarca de Manaus. Em caso de descumprimento da ordem de paralisação, foi estabelecida multa diária de R$ 100 mil, destinada a programas ambientais, sem prejuízo de eventual responsabilização criminal.

O incêndio começou em 6 de outubro de 2026 e atingiu uma área superior a 15 mil metros quadrados, segundo informações citadas na decisão. O fogo provocou uma densa nuvem de fumaça, com impactos na qualidade do ar e riscos à saúde pública.

MP aponta suspeita de irregularidades ambientais

A ação do MPAM foi baseada em informações reunidas durante a apuração do caso. Segundo o órgão, dados preliminares do Instituto de Proteção Ambiental do Amazonas (Ipaam) indicaram que a licença concedida para o empreendimento autorizava apenas o armazenamento de resíduos inertes.

No entanto, havia suspeita de que o local também armazenava materiais inflamáveis ou combustíveis, o que motivou o pedido de suspensão das autorizações e das atividades.

Na decisão, a Justiça considerou o cenário de intensa fumaça em Manaus, os riscos à saúde pública, a necessidade de evacuação de trabalhadores da região e a atuação contínua do Corpo de Bombeiros no combate ao incêndio.

O g1 questionou o posicionamento dos proprietários, mas até a atualização mais recente desta reportagem não obteve resposta.

Incêndio atinge vegetação em Manaus. — Foto: William Duarte/Rede Amazônica

A suspensão das atividades não se aplica às ações emergenciais necessárias para reduzir os riscos no local. Segundo a decisão, devem continuar os trabalhos de combate a focos remanescentes, rescaldo, controle de poluentes e demais medidas determinadas pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e pelo Ipaam.

O instituto ambiental também deverá fiscalizar o cumprimento da ordem judicial e registrar a suspensão das licenças em seus sistemas.

A decisão determina ainda que a 50ª Promotoria de Justiça Especializada na Proteção do Meio Ambiente e Patrimônio Histórico (Prodemaph), sob responsabilidade da promotora Lílian Maria Pires Stone, dê continuidade à investigação e obtenha os documentos e as informações necessários para a instrução do processo.

articles.title: On lines of US, India ‘developing integrated defence logistics system for tri services’ that will support planned theatre commands
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a move to integrate defence logistics infrastructure that will help in seamless coordination among three services, especially during
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a move to integrate defence logistics infrastructure that will help in seamless coordination among three services, especially during conflicts, the Union govt is developing an integrated logistics structure on the lines of the US to support its planned theatre commands.The details of the project, being spearheaded by the department of military affairs (DMA), have been explained in a letter that Rear Admiral Kunal Singh Rajkumar, a joint secretary (navy and defence staff) in DMA, wrote to Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade in response to his missive to PM Narendra Modi in which the latter gave suggestions for “examining a unified defence logistics and fuel management framework on the lines of the US Defence Logistics Agency”.In his letter, MP Gopchade has drawn attention to the functioning of US DLA, which serves as a single centralised combat logistics support agency for the entire US department of defence. US DLA manages fuel supply, military procurement, spare parts, logistics AI systems, defence standardisation, petroleum quality assurance, warehousing, technical support, and global supply-chain management under an integrated tri-service structure. He also told PM that at present, logistics management in India is largely distributed across multiple service-specific structures such as Army Service Corps, Army Ordnance Corps, EME, Naval logistics branches, Air Force maintenance systems, fuel depots and various procurement and inventory mechanisms.Talking to TOI, Gopchade said DMA has informed him that “all best practices relevant in India’s context are being incorporated in creation of an integrated logistics structure to support planned theatre commands”. To give proper shape to the proposal, he has been told that “joint operations logistics committee (JOLC), joint services study group (JSSGs), joint working groups (JWGs) and inter-service maintenance working groups (IMWGs) have been constituted at appropriate levels to integrate logistics process and procedures among the services.”The MP further told TOI DMA has informed him “tri-services logistics management application is also under development to provide real time inter-service inventory visibility and to integrate service specific enterprise resource planning software”. He was also briefed in the letter that “work on the National Defence Codification System is also under way and that joint logistics node and subsequently joint ammunition depots, air stores supply parks and material organisations are being planned pan-India”.The PM Gati Shakti defence portal is also under development to align with National Logistics Policy and Unified Logistics Interface Platform for providing a defence-equivalent ‘joint logistics interface’ across three services and theatre boundaries. Furthermore, emerging AI and machine learning technologies are being incorporated for logistic optimisation. A joint logistics integration, akin to US DLA, is a strategic imperative for the country and its realisation is a prime priority for the defence ministry, he was told.In his letter to the PM, MP Gopchade had suggested a slew of reforms such as setting up of a unified defence fuel management system, introduction of a secure military fuel card system, an AI-enabled predictive logistics and maintenance and integrated petroleum quality assurance network.

articles.title: Wildfire races through SoCal, burning homes as mass evacuations ordered
articles.summary: A wildfire exploded in Orange County on Friday, forcing evacuations as it burned several homes and threatened dozens more. The Norte Fire broke out around 11...
articles.body:
A wildfire exploded in Orange County on Friday, forcing evacuations as it burned several homes and threatened dozens more.

The Norte Fire broke out around 11:30 a.m. in the San Clemente area, growing to 465 acres in about three hours, according to the Orange County Fire Authority and CalFire .

The OCFA later confirmed that six homes had been damaged or destroyed in the blaze, having earlier cited four "impacted" homes off Via La Mira in San Juan Capistrano.

A firefighter suffered heat exhaustion, but no other injuries were reported.

Aerial footage from KTLA showed several homes burning as the fire appeared to threaten several more.

"Crews are aggressively attacking the fire from the ground and air. Please continue to avoid the area," CalFire wrote in an update.

Evacuation orders were issued for San Juan Zones 4, 5, and 10 as well as San Clemente Zones 12 and 13.

Evacuation shelters were set up at the San Juan Capistrano Community Center and the San Clemente Community Center.

Heat, strong winds, and dry conditions were fueling the blaze as firefighters and aerial support worked to stop its spread.

Nine schools in the Capistrano Unified School District dismissed students early due to the blaze, after earlier telling students to stay indoors due to the smoke.

San Clemente Mayor Rick Loeffler told KTLA the city had been making preparations for a fire.

"We actually instituted a goat program about a year ago, a pilot program to have goats start clearing our hillsides," he said.

"The county supplied a pumpkin tank at the top of our ridge, which allows helicopters to come in and resupply their water quickly."

The fire was one of several burning in Southern California on Friday.

The Bryson Fire was ripping through the hills north of Malibu , burning 147 acres as of early Friday evening.

The blaze burned just north of Encinal Canyon Road and was threatening the LA County juvenile detention facility Camp Fred Miller to its east and the Malibu Country Club to its west.

Malibu officials were not aware of any homes damaged or destroyed by the fire. One firefighter was under unknown circumstances.

The city remains still under a Red Flag Warning and a heat advisory until Saturday at 8 p.m.

Ongoing Red Flag Warnings in effect across much of Los Angeles and Ventura counties have signaled ideal conditions for fires to break out.

Meanwhile, the Henderson Fire near Camp Pendleton in San Diego had scorched more than 2,000 acres as of early Friday evening, with 17% containment.

articles.title: Seca compromete safra de macaxeira e afeta produção de farinha em RR | G1
articles.standfirst: No município de Iracema, ao Sul de Roraima, a falta de chuva interrompeu temporariamente a produção de farinha do produtor rural Jair Mota, de 63 anos.
articles.summary: No município de Iracema, ao Sul de Roraima, a falta de chuva interrompeu temporariamente a produção de farinha do produtor rural Jair Mota, de 63 anos.
articles.body:
A estiagem e a falta de chuvas têm afetado o cultivo da macaxeira e a produção de farinha , um dos principais alimentos da região Norte. No município de Iracema, ao Sul de Roraima, a falta de chuva interrompeu temporariamente a produção de farinha do produtor rural Jair Mota, de 63 anos.

📈 Em Boa Vista , o preço da mandioca subiu 5,7% em setembro, chegando a R$ 35 por 6 kg . Já a farinha teve aumento de 3,06%, com o preço de R$ 22,23 por 3 kg , conforme dados da Secretaria de Planejamento e Orçamento de Roraima (Seplan).

A seca prejudicou o desenvolvimento das plantas e reduziu a produtividade da lavoura de Jair, que trabalha com o cultivo de mandioca há cerca de três anos.

"Estamos no período de entressafra, por causa da seca. Fizemos um replantio no final do período chuvoso. Agora, está tudo plantado para colher no ano que vem e produzir farinha. A produtividade cai porque não tem umidade, e a raiz da mandioca necessita de água para crescer e se desenvolver. A quantidade de amido diminui porque tem pouco líquido no solo", afirmou.

Seca compromete safra de macaxeira e afeta produção de farinha em Roraima — Foto: Nalu Cardoso/g1 RR

A previsão do produtor é retomar a colheita entre março e maio de 2027, com a chegada das chuvas. Até lá, a produção permanece parada.

Jair afirma que a situação também afeta outros produtores rurais que vivem em lotes no interior do estado. Segundo ele, a falta de chuva dificulta o plantio, a colheita e até a criação de animais. A irrigação ajuda a reduzir os prejuízos em algumas propriedades, mas não resolve o problema de todos.

Para manter a renda durante o período sem produção, o produtor recorre a outras atividades comerciais. "Tem que buscar outra alternativa de negócio para sobreviver. Eu tenho outras empresas e outros negócios, que não estão necessariamente ligados à plantação", disse.

Alta no preço da farinha afeta produção em Boa Vista

A empresa de farofa Sabor do Norte, de João Botelho, de 35 anos, compra farinha amarela de mandioca do Amazonas . Na fábrica, em Boa Vista, o produto é torrado com ingredientes naturais e embalado.

A marca trabalha com as linhas tradicional e ovinha, nos sabores manteiga, pimenta Uarini e bacon. As farofas são distribuídas em 14 dos 15 municípios de Roraima, com exceção de Uiramutã. Além disso, os produtos são comercializados em São Paulo e Santa Catarina e também exportados para os Estados Unidos.

🔍 A farinha ovinha, também conhecida como farinha de Uarini, é um alimento tradicional da Amazônia, originário do município de Uarini, no Amazonas. O produto é declarado Patrimônio Cultural de Natureza Imaterial do estado.

A produção diária da empresa varia de 400 a 500 unidades, com o uso de aproximadamente 300 quilos de farinha. A fábrica funciona de segunda a sexta-feira e produz cerca de 2,5 mil unidades de farofa por semana .

João Botelho, dono da empresa Sabor do Norte — Foto: Nalu Cardoso/g1 RR

O empresário mantém um estoque elevado para se preparar para o período de estiagem no fim do ano, mas não esperava uma seca tão intensa. Segundo ele, deve manter o preço atual até fevereiro de 2027, enquanto o clima não estabiliza.

"Comprávamos a tonelada por cerca de R$ 6,7 mil. Agora, o valor varia entre R$ 9 mil e R$ 10 mil, mas chegou a R$ 12 mil", disse.

O empresário afirma que, além da redução da produção de farinha, a baixa dos rios no Amazonas encarece o transporte da matéria-prima .

"Roraima ainda tem uma participação muito pequena na produção de farinha. Lá [no Amazonas], o que mais impacta é o frete, porque, quando o rio seca, o transporte fica mais caro", explicou.

De acordo com o Observatório da Indústria da Federação das Indústrias do Estado de Roraima (Fier), o frete em Roraima pode ficar até 50% mais caro no fim de 2026 e no início de 2027 por causa do El Niño.

"Toda vez que chega o período de final de ano, entre outubro e dezembro, os rios começam a baixar na região do Amazonas e a farinha sofre uma elevação de preço. Esse fenômeno acontece todos os anos, mas, desta vez, tivemos o El Niño e, além da seca dos rios, houve uma diminuição da produção por falta de chuva", afirmou João.

ENTENDA: O El Niño é um fenômeno climático caracterizado pelo aquecimento anormal das águas superficiais do Oceano Pacífico Equatorial. O fenômeno deve ganhar força no segundo semestre de 2026 e pode persistir até o início de 2027. Em Roraima, pode contribuir para períodos mais quentes e secos, alterar o regime de chuvas e aumentar o risco de incêndios florestais.

A combinação de calor intenso, falta de chuvas e baixa umidade do ar elevou o perigo de incêndios florestais em Roraima . Uma previsão do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) indica que as precipitações continuarão escassas e mal distribuídas até pelo menos o fim de outubro.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo BH: Chuva forte atinge capital e região no sábado | G1
articles.standfirst: BH e região metropolitana podem ter chuva forte neste sábado; veja a previsão
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo em BH indica pancadas de chuva forte e temperaturas entre 18°C e 27°C neste sábado devido à passagem de uma frente fria pelo Sudeste.
articles.body:
BH e região metropolitana podem ter chuva forte neste sábado; veja a previsão — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Belo Horizonte e a região metropolitana podem registrar pancadas de chuva fortes neste sábado (17), segundo o Climatempo. O tempo deve continuar instável no domingo (18), quando a chuva é esperada principalmente à tarde e à noite.

Na capital, a previsão para este sábado é de temperaturas entre 18°C e 27°C. O sol aparece entre nuvens, mas há possibilidade de chuva durante o dia e à noite. A probabilidade de chover é de 97%, com acumulado estimado de 15,2 milímetros.

A instabilidade está associada à passagem de uma frente fria pelo Sudeste. Segundo o Climatempo, o sistema, combinado com o ar quente e úmido, favorece a formação de nuvens carregadas. A previsão divulgada na sexta-feira (16) aponta possibilidade de pancadas fortes na Grande BH neste sábado.

Em Betim, as temperaturas devem variar entre 19°C e 27°C neste sábado. A previsão é de períodos de sol entre nuvens, com chuvas passageiras durante o dia e à noite. A chance de chover é de 91%, com volume estimado de 5,5 milímetros.

Contagem também tem previsão de sol entre nuvens e chuva ao longo do sábado, inclusive à noite. Os termômetros devem marcar entre 18°C e 26°C. A probabilidade de chuva é de 94%, com acumulado previsto de 6,4 milímetros.

O domingo pode começar com períodos de sol em Belo Horizonte e na região metropolitana. A abertura no tempo, porém, não deve durar o dia inteiro: a previsão indica novas pancadas de chuva à tarde e à noite.

Em BH, os termômetros devem marcar entre 19°C e 27°C. A probabilidade de chuva é de 69%, com volume estimado de 5,1 milímetros — abaixo do previsto para sábado.

Em Betim, o domingo deve ter sol entre muitas nuvens pela manhã e pancadas de chuva à tarde. À noite, a previsão indica tempo sem chuva. As temperaturas ficam entre 17°C e 28°C, com probabilidade de chuva de 77% e acumulado estimado de 1,6 milímetro.

Já em Contagem, há previsão de pancadas à tarde e à noite, com temperaturas entre 18°C e 27°C. A chance de chover é de 81%, e o volume previsto é de 1,9 milímetro.

articles.title: Murder in Malaysia: Justice for Altantuya Shaariibuu
articles.summary: 101 East investigates if power and politics are shielding those behind the 2006 murder of a Mongolian woman in Malaysia.
articles.body:
Twenty years ago, two Malaysian special forces policemen brutally murdered Mongolian woman Altantuya Shaariibuu, obliterating her body with C4 military explosives.

But the truth behind why they killed her has yet to be determined, leading to suspicions of a political conspiracy to silence her.

101 East travels to Mongolia, Malaysia, France and Australia to investigate allegations of interference in the criminal trial, Altantuya’s suspected links to an allegedly corrupt submarine deal and claims by the policemen that they acted on the orders of convicted former Prime Minister Najib Razak, who vehemently denies any involvement in the murder.

articles.title: Influencers seguem divulgando bets e 'Tigrinho' após proibição federal | G1
articles.standfirst: O g1 verificou que, pelo menos, 40 perfis usam os stories do Instagram para divulgar os links das plataformas. Medida Provisória proibiu a exploração e a publicidade das apostas no país.
articles.summary: O g1 verificou que, pelo menos, 40 perfis usam os stories do Instagram para divulgar os links das plataformas. Medida Provisória proibiu a exploração e a publicidade das apostas.
articles.body:
Influenciadores digitais do Ceará continuam a divulgar bets e cassinos virtuais mesmo após as plataformas serem proibidas pelo governo federal. O g1 verificou que, pelo menos, 40 perfis usam os stories do Instagram para divulgar os links das plataformas.

No dia 25 de setembro, a proibição foi determinada pela Medida Provisória (MP) nº 1.394 . A medida proibiu a exploração, a oferta, a intermediação e a publicidade das apostas de quota fixa no Brasil. A regra também vale para os jogos on-line e os chamados cassinos virtuais, como o Jogo do Tigrinho.

As bets pararam de funcionar no país, na teoria, a partir do dia 6 de outubro. O g1 entrou em dezenas de perfis de influenciadores do Ceará entre os dias 10 e 13 de outubro, após a proibição. A reportagem flagrou que os 40 influencers seguiram divulgando as plataformas de maneira explícita , em perfis abertos com milhares de seguidores, sem sequer citar a proibição do governo federal.

Entre os perfis, estão influenciadores como Nayara Souza, Italo Wendel (conhecido como Belo Belo) e Jéssica Santos (conhecida como Jessica Macaxeira). Todos acumulam mais de um milhão de seguidores nas redes sociais .

Jéssica Santos respondeu ao g1 que está ciente da Medida Provisória, mas "tinha contratos em andamento que precisava cumprir, e sempre prezei pela responsabilidade e pelo compromisso com aquilo que assumo". A influenciadora ponderou que reconhece "o quanto os jogos de apostas têm feito mal à vida de tantas pessoas e famílias". "Por isso, decidi que irei cumprir apenas até o fim do meu contrato", garantiu (leia a resposta da influenciadora na íntegra abaixo) .

O g1 entrou em contato também com os outros dois influenciadores, mas não recebeu resposta até a publicação desta reportagem.

Alguns dos perfis divulgam as bets e cassinos virtuais até mesmo com publicações onde vincularam as próprias imagens às plataformas, colocando vídeos e fotos junto aos links que variam entre “tigrinhos”, “coelhinhos”, “tourinhos” e outros mascotes dos jogos de azar .

Influenciadores com mais de 1 milhão de seguidores divulgam apostas após proibição desse tipo de divulgação. — Foto: Reprodução.

A divulgação das plataformas de apostas no Brasil não se tornou crime com a publicação MP 1.394. No entanto, o texto da medida proibiu a publicidade dos jogos com base no Código de Defesa do Consumidor. Assim, a divulgação das plataformas configura publicidade abusiva, sujeitando os infratores às sanções administrativas.

➡️Uma Medida Provisória (MP) é um instrumento legal utilizado pelo presidente da República para estabelecer regras com força de lei em situações de relevância e urgência. A MP entra em vigor imediatamente após a publicação, mas precisa ser aprovada pelo Congresso Nacional, no prazo de até 60 dias, prorrogável uma vez, para se tornar lei definitiva. Caso não seja aprovada dentro do prazo, perde a validade, conforme as regras da Constituição Federal.

“Ficam vedadas, no território nacional, as ações de comunicação, de publicidade, de propaganda, de marketing e de patrocínio relativas a loterias de aposta de quota fixa, em qualquer meio de comunicação, físico ou digital”.

A punição ao influenciador que segue divulgando as plataformas de apostas pode variar de acordo com cada caso, como explica a advogada Raquel Andrade.

“A sanção administrativa é o ponto de partida. Essas sanções administrativas, fiscais, possível aplicação de multa, possível retirada do perfil, possível retirada da publicidade, a possível solicitação de perdas e danos de direitos sobre os danos morais e materiais causados, a possível cobrança retroativa de impostos, multas administrativas, tudo isso pode ser aplicado”, detalhou.

Para Andrade, o caráter da proibição feito por medida provisória deu aos influenciadores que divulgam as plataformas uma “sensação de falsa impunidade” .

“Então, um influencer que não se sensibiliza com notícias de suicídio de jovens, de trabalhadores, o fato de que bilhões de reais estão saindo do orçamento para comida, para lazer, para escola, para moradia, e que, no fim das contas, só está interessado em lucrar, porque é o lucro da desgraça, lucrar em cima da tragédia alheia, eu acho que isso fala mais do influencer do que da própria lei, do que da própria norma”, criticou a advogada.

O governo federal enviou ao Congresso um projeto de lei para tornar crime tanto a exploração quanto a publicidade de bets . Os crimes previstos no texto são:

explorar ou operar apostas de quota fixa: pena de 4 a 6 anos de reclusão e multa;

divulgar apostas ou captar apostadores: pena de 2 a 4 anos de reclusão e multa;

usar dados pessoais para captar apostadores: pena de 2 a 4 anos e multa;

facilitar financeiramente a exploração: pena de 2 a 4 anos e multa;

fornecer aplicação de internet para apostas: pena de 2 a 4 anos e multa, com agravantes em determinadas situações.

Em nota enviada ao g1 , o Ministério da Fazenda disse que a Secretaria de Prêmio e Apostas (SPA/MF) fiscaliza os sites de apostas , de acordo com a Medida Provisória 1.394/2026.

“A busca por sites ilegais é contínua e feita por meio de um laboratório virtual e pela equipe técnica da SPA, que monitora buscadores, deep web, dark web, denúncias e ouvidorias”, comentou a pasta.

O órgão ministerial explicou que, quando um site que potencialmente oferece apostas é identificado, a equipe verifica se há de fato oferta ilegal. “Constatada a irregularidade, a URL é enviada à Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel), que aciona os provedores de internet para realizar o bloqueio”, detalhou.

“Em paralelo, a Secretaria identifica os meios de pagamento aceitos por esses sites e determina o bloqueio das contas financeiras usadas na operação. A fiscalização de redes sociais e de aplicativos em lojas online é de competência do Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, conforme a MP”, complementou.

O g1 também procurou o Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública e a Polícia Federal para entender as investigações e possíveis implicações criminais. A PF comentou que não vai responder sobre a atuação no combate às bets, enquanto o Ministério não emitiu resposta à demanda até a publicação desta matéria.

Site de uma casa de apostas bloqueado — Foto: Isabela Ortiz/g1

O psicólogo Magnum Freire comentou que a divulgação de plataformas ilegais, especialmente por influenciadores, pode ter um impacto na saúde mental da população ainda pior do que com as bets e cassinos virtuais regulamentados.

“Nos ambientes ilegais não há direcionamento automático do usuário para canal de apoio nenhum, então a busca sobre terapia ou até atendimento psiquiátrico para ludopatia vai ser inócua, não vai existir, isolando cada vez mais o indivíduo e reduzindo as portas de entrada para o tratamento”, afirma.

O cunho da ilegalidade vinculado às plataformas proibidas pode, inclusive, impactar a percepção social do próprio jogador. “[...] desenvolve uma vergonha extrema escondendo o problema da família, das pessoas que ele gosta, até atingir a ruína total. Isso adia severamente o momento da busca por auxílio terapêutico”, destaca o psicólogo.

Magnum explicou que a influência obtida por esses perfis, que acumulam milhares de seguidores, cumpre papel imperioso na vontade de apostar.

“[O apostador] vê aquela pessoa com um estilo desejável, ganhando um ‘dinheiro fácil’ . Isso ativa, no apostador, o que a gente chama de ‘aprendizagem vicária’. A sensação falsa de que o sucesso do outro é replicado de uma forma instantânea, muito rápida, e não vai ter atalho para isso. Erroneamente, ele vai pensar que apostando vai conseguir aquilo”, reforçou o psicólogo.

O que disse a influenciadora Jéssica Macaxeira

"Estou ciente da MP [Medida Provisória], sim! Mas eu tinha contratos em andamento que precisava cumprir, e sempre prezei pela responsabilidade e pelo compromisso com aquilo que assumo. Por isso, optei por cumprir minhas obrigações contratuais até o fim, mas não darei continuidade após esses contratos.

Reconheço o quanto os jogos de apostas têm feito mal à vida de tantas pessoas e famílias. Por isso, decidi que irei cumprir apenas até o fim do meu contrato.

Ao mesmo tempo, acredito que simplesmente proibir não resolve o problema do vício, porque quem sofre com essa dependência pode acabar buscando outros caminhos para continuar apostando. Não basta proibir, é preciso cuidar, acolher e oferecer caminhos para a recuperação.

Precisamos de medidas que ajudem essas pessoas a saírem desse ciclo, com apoio psicológico, tratamento e acompanhamento. Afinal, por trás de cada pessoa viciada, existe uma história, uma família e, muitas vezes, alguém que precisa de ajuda para recomeçar."

articles.title: Qualidade do ar em Manaus atinge nível perigoso por queimadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Por volta das 6h, a capital amazonense registrava 441 pontos no índice de qualidade do ar, o pior resultado entre as capitais brasileiras em tempo real.
articles.summary: Qualidade do ar em Manaus registrou 441 pontos neste sábado, tornando-se a capital mais poluída do país devido à fumaça das queimadas na região.
articles.body:
A fumaça provocada pelas queimadas deixou a qualidade do ar em Manaus em nível "perigoso" na manhã deste sábado (17). A concentração de partículas finas de poluição chegou a 59,2 vezes o valor recomendado pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) para a média anual desse poluente, segundo a plataforma internacional IQAir.

Por volta das 6h, a capital amazonense registrava 441 pontos no índice de qualidade do ar , o pior resultado entre as capitais brasileiras em tempo real . O principal poluente identificado era o material particulado fino (PM2.5), com concentração de 295,9 microgramas por metro cúbico (µg/m³) .

A OMS recomenda que a média anual de PM2.5 não ultrapasse 5 µg/m³. O valor registrado em Manaus naquele momento era 59,2 vezes maior que essa referência.

A diferença em relação à segunda capital mais poluída do ranking também era expressiva. Porto Velho (RO) registrava 65 pontos no índice de qualidade do ar, contra 441 em Manaus, segundo a IQAir.

Os dados do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva), da Universidade do Estado do Amazonas ( UEA ), também indicavam piora na qualidade do ar. Por volta das 6h55, os índices eram classificados como "péssimo" nos pontos monitorados da capital. Em um deles, a concentração de partículas chegou a 457,7 µg/m³ , no bairro Coroado.

🔎 A qualidade do ar é considerada boa pelo Selva quando a concentração de partículas fica entre 0 e 25 µg/m³ . Acima desse nível, os índices passam por classificações que variam de moderada a péssimo, conforme a escala utilizada pelo sistema.

Moradores relatam fumaça intensa e dificuldade para respirar

Nas redes sociais, moradores de Manaus relataram cheiro forte de fumaça, ardência nos olhos e dificuldade para respirar neste sábado. Algumas publicações descreveram o episódio como o pior já vivido na capital.

"Mais um dia acordando com o fedor insuportável de fumaça. a qualidade do ar em manaus continua péssima e, mais uma vez, volto a dizer que sinto que estão tentando nos matar sufocados", escreveu um usuário na rede social X.

Outro morador relatou que a fumaça prejudicava a visibilidade: "Hoje de longe o pior dia pra se estar em Manaus, a fumaça é tão forte, fedorenta e densa que até a visibilidade tá afetada".

"O pior limiar de todos os episódios de fumaça na cidade", publicou outra pessoa.

Também houve relatos de ardência nos olhos mesmo dentro de casa e críticas à atuação das autoridades. "Arrisco dizer que hoje é o pior dia de Manaus no quesito poluição, os olhos ardem dentro de casa. E o pior: os governantes não estão levando o assunto tão a sério como deveria ser", escreveu um usuário.

Outras publicações apontaram a percepção de piora ao longo dos dias. "Parece que Manaus amanhece cada dia pior com essa fumaça", afirmou uma pessoa.

Em outra mensagem, um usuário descreveu a dificuldade para respirar na capital: "Manaus, 17 de outubro de 2026. tá dificílimo respirar, uma forte fumaça se espalhou por toda a cidade".

Municípios do Amazonas também registram altos índices de poluição

A poluição também atingiu níveis elevados em municípios do interior do Amazonas, segundo dados do Selva. Por volta das 6h10 , Maués registrava concentração de 750,5 µg/m³, enquanto Urucurituba tinha 560,4 µg/m³ e Itacoatiara , 413 µg/m³.

No mesmo horário, os índices eram de 259,9 µg/m³ em Boa Vista do Ramos , 257,8 µg/m³ em Itapiranga e 123,2 µg/m³ em Silves .

Por volta das 7h16 , Urucurituba registrava 731,1 µg/m³, e Maués, 724,7 µg/m³. Em Autazes , a concentração chegou a 607,3 µg/m³. Manaquiri tinha 468,5 µg/m³, Itacoatiara, 475,8 µg/m³, e Iranduba , 407,7 µg/m³.

Também foram registrados 278,1 µg/m³ em Itapiranga, 262,2 µg/m³ em Careiro da Várzea , 235,4 µg/m³ em Silves e 226,9 µg/m³ em Boa Vista do Ramos.

articles.summary: Santos, Praia Grande, Guarujá e Itanhaém terão Papanicolau, encaminhamento para mamografia, vacinação e outros procedimentos. Parte dos atendimentos exige agendamento prévio.
articles.body:
A programação do outubro rosa contempla quatro cidades da Baixada Santista. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Santos

Mulheres de Santos , Praia Grande , Guarujá e Itanhaém , no litoral de São Paulo, poderão participar de ações de saúde neste sábado (17), como parte da programação do Outubro Rosa. Entre os serviços oferecidos estão exames preventivos, encaminhamentos para mamografia, vacinação e palestras.

As atividades fazem parte da campanha de conscientização sobre a prevenção e o diagnóstico precoce dos cânceres de mama e do colo do útero. Parte dos procedimentos exige agendamento prévio, por isso as pacientes devem verificar as condições de atendimento antes de comparecer às unidades.

As policlínicas municipais de Santos terão programação especial das 9h às 15h30, com palestras, rodas de conversa, atividades físicas, exames preventivos e vacinação. Confira as ações por unidade:

Também haverá vacinação itinerante na Praça Almirante Gago Coutinho, na Ponta da Praia, das 10h às 16h. É necessário apresentar a carteira de vacinação ou um documento com foto. Já o Complexo Hospitalar dos Estivadores (CHE) realizará mamografias das 9h30 às 18h50, exclusivamente para pacientes previamente agendadas.

O Instituto da Mulher – Casa Rosa, na Vila Maia, realizará um mutirão das 8h às 17h para pacientes previamente agendadas que aguardavam atendimento na rede municipal. Estão previstos 85 procedimentos, distribuídos da seguinte forma:

Outro mutirão está previsto para sábado (24), com os mesmos procedimentos e atendimentos ginecológicos. A expectativa da prefeitura é atender cerca de 165 pacientes nessa segunda etapa.

As 31 Unidades de Saúde da Família (Usafas) de Praia Grande funcionarão das 9h às 16h, com coleta de Papanicolau, avaliação clínica para encaminhamento à mamografia, consultas e outros procedimentos. Também haverá atendimento odontológico e inserção de dispositivo intrauterino (DIU) e Implanon, mediante agendamento e conforme os protocolos municipais.

Para receber atendimento, é necessário apresentar documento com foto e cartão da unidade. No caso do Papanicolau, a paciente não deve estar menstruada e precisa evitar relações sexuais, cremes e duchas vaginais nos dois dias anteriores ao exame.

Entre segunda (19) e sexta-feira (23), as Usafas também terão horário estendido, das 17h às 19h, para ampliar o acesso das mulheres aos serviços de saúde.

Outubro Rosa reforça a importância da prevenção, do acompanhamento médico e da detecção precoce do câncer de mama — Foto: Reprodução/Magnific

O Centro Especializado na Saúde da Criança e da Mulher (Cescrim) realizará inserções de Implanon das 7h às 16h. A unidade fica na Avenida Tiradentes, 184, no Jardim Mosteiro.

Já a Unidade de Saúde da Família (USF) Gaivota terá programação das 9h às 15h, com café da manhã, coleta de exames preventivos e outras atividades. O endereço é Avenida Flácides Ferreira, 500, no bairro Gaivota.

articles.title: Tony Hawk founded a nonprofit in 2002 to expand access to free public skateparks; it has since helped fund nearly 700 parks across all 50 US states
articles.summary: For young skateboarders, finding a safe, legal place to practise is not always easy.
articles.body: For young skateboarders, finding a safe, legal place to practise is not always easy. Since 2002, a nonprofit founded by professional skateboarder Tony Hawk has helped communities develop public skateparks, particularly in areas with limited recreational facilities. Formerly known as the Tony Hawk Foundation, the organisation became The Skatepark Project in 2020 to put its mission at the centre of its identity. It provides grants, technical assistance and other resources to communities seeking to create free public skating spaces. The organisation says it has helped fund nearly 700 skateparks across all 50 US states. A February 2026 Los Angeles City Council report separately documents its involvement in a skateboarding facility at the West Los Angeles Municipal Complex. Its work includes permanent community parks and temporary facilities developed with municipal authorities. Examples from Augusta, Kansas, and Los Angeles show how nonprofit support can help expand access to public recreation.The Skatepark Project: how Tony Hawk’s foundation began in 2002Hawk established the nonprofit to address the shortage of public places where young people could skateboard legally. According to The Skatepark Project’s account, Hawk used the $125,000 he won on Who Wants to Be a Millionaire in 2001 to help launch the organisation. It was formally founded in 2002 as the Tony Hawk Foundation. The foundation focused on helping communities secure funding and other resources for public skateparks, especially in underserved areas. Rather than limiting its work to financial assistance, it developed a community-oriented approach involving local advocates, public authorities and skatepark users.In 2020, the foundation adopted the name The Skatepark Project. A 2020 announcement about the rebranding reported that the organisation had helped fund more than 600 public skateparks across all 50 states. Its current programmes include grants of up to $25,000 for eligible projects, as well as technical assistance and support for youth activities. The organisation’s grant guidelines specify that projects must provide permanent, public concrete skateparks in underserved communities, remain free to use and involve local users in planning, fundraising and design. The organisation’s grant guidelines also set requirements for community support and project funding.Free skateparks in underserved communities: how grants and local funding workThe emphasis on free access is central to the organisation’s mission. A public skatepark does not require users to pay an entry fee or purchase a membership, although skaters may still need their own equipment. The Skatepark Project’s support is intended to help communities create facilities where young people can participate without the cost of private recreational venues. One of its regional initiatives is Built to Play, a partnership with the Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation. The Built to Play initiative, a partnership with the Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation, aimed to support up to 20 public skateparks across 16 counties in Southeast Michigan and Western New York. A separate example comes from Augusta, Kansas. In an announcement about a $15,000 grant from The Skatepark Project, the city said the funding would help address potential construction-cost increases for its community skatepark. The city also described plans to pursue additional funding and continue local fundraising.The Augusta project subsequently opened to the public on 5 November 2023, according to the city’s skatepark opening announcement. The example illustrates the wider role of municipal planning and community investment in establishing public recreational facilities. The Built to Play initiative and Augusta’s grant are separate examples of the organisation’s work, rather than parts of the same programme. The organisation’s reported national reach should be distinguished from estimates of park usage. Published figures for annual visits vary, and the available material does not establish whether they use comparable dates or counting methods. These estimates should therefore not be presented as a verified count of unique visitors.Los Angeles skate plaza: a $70,000 donation accepted in 2026The organisation’s work also includes temporary facilities developed with local authorities. In Los Angeles, the City Council considered a donation valued at approximately $70,000 for skateboarding features at the West Los Angeles Municipal Complex. The city’s official council record confirms that the council adopted the Government Operations Committee report on 3 February 2026, with all recorded votes in favour. The donation comprised labour, materials and equipment for four skate obstacles, handrails, ledges, a wedge spine, signage and replicas of courthouse monuments.Under the proposal, the Skatepark Project would oversee the design and construction with professional builders and cover the associated costs. The improvements were intended to provide a temporary skating facility while the complex remained subject to redevelopment plans. A local report described new features and murals being unveiled at the site on 3 February 2026, the same day the City Council adopted the committee report. The Los Angeles example shows that the organisation’s role can extend beyond conventional grants. It can contribute equipment, construction resources and project oversight to help create skating opportunities at existing public sites.Across its programmes, The Skatepark Project combines grant funding, technical assistance and partnerships with communities and public agencies. Its reported national reach provides a measure of the scale of its work, while local examples show how individual facilities depend on planning, funding and construction. articles.title: Takaichi says chores, makeup add hours to her workday, sparks debate on gender roles
articles.summary: TOKYO: Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi’s comments that she works longer than her male predecessors because of household chores and makeup have sparked debate
articles.body: TOKYO: Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi’s comments that she works longer than her male predecessors because of household chores and makeup have sparked debate over gender roles and work-life balance in Japan.Addressing parliament Wednesday, Takaichi described the additional demands she faces as a woman. “In the morning, I take a bath, fix breakfast and do the dishes, then apply makeup,” she said. “Doing these things, I feel I’m spending three or four more hours than male prime ministers.”She said aides took time to realise she needed extra time to apply makeup and prepare for television appearances. Her remarks drew criticism for reinforcing traditional gender roles and normalising excessive working hours. Govt figures show women spend nearly five hours daily on housework, against about 40 minutes for an average man.Takaichi, who took office last year, has said she sleeps between zero and three hours a night because of homemaking responsibilities and her official workload. Critics said she was setting a poor example on work-life balance and gender equality.Fumitake Fujita, a senior official of junior coalition partner Japan Innovation Party, raised the issue of PM’s schedule Wednesday, suggesting that hours-long parliamentary sessions, which ministers attend almost daily, be reduced. Citing NXJI Research, he said Japan’s PM attended parliamentary sessions on 72 days in 2022, compared with 50 in Britain and 13 in Germany.Takaichi said she routinely takes home documents despite difficulty managing her schedule. “I do enjoy reading them late at night,” she said. “Honestly, I feel it is not easy to squeeze out time to sit down and think about the future direction of Japan or have a grand vision.”You use AI every day. articles.title: A 7am email to employer, ‘I love you’ on clothes and a chilling ‘leaving this world’ note on wife’s birthday: What preceded Malayali techie couple’s deaths in Gurgaon flat
articles.summary: GURGAON: An email sent to his employer at around 7am, saying “we are leaving this world”, set off a chain of events that led to the discovery of an IT
articles.body: GURGAON: An email sent to his employer at around 7am, saying “we are leaving this world”, set off a chain of events that led to the discovery of an IT professional and his wife dead in their Gurgaon apartment on Wednesday.The techie had also shared the phone numbers of his parents and landlord, asking the company to inform them.When the landlord reached the flat in Tower 7 of M3M Marina, he found Mohammad Aslam (30) hanging and his wife, Farhana, who was about to turn 28, lying on the floor with an injury mark on her neck. He alerted Badshapur police station.Inside the flat, police found a note bearing the words “We are leaving this world”. The words “I love you” had also been scribbled on Farhana's clothes. Investigators are examining the messages and other material recovered from the apartment as they piece together what led to the couple’s deaths.Police suspect Aslam killed Farhana before dying by suicide, but said the sequence of events and the cause of death had not yet been established. A murder case was registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The couple’s families, based in Kerala, have been left struggling to understand what happened. Relatives said they knew of no marital discord and described the couple as being close to each other. They said Aslam had been undergoing treatment for depression for around a year and a half.“The couple shared a really close bond. Both were happy with each other and had no marital discord. There was no issue with the family either. But hearing this has left both families in shock,” said Faisal, Farhana’s brother.Moved to Gurgaon three months agoThe couple had relocated to Gurgaon from Bengaluru around three months ago. Aslam, a native of Kozhikode, had joined an Indonesia-based IT company with an office in Sector 58. Farhana, who hailed from Malappuram, worked from home for an IT firm based in Bengaluru.They married in 2023 and spent around two years in Bengaluru before moving to Gurgaon.Aslam graduated in electrical and electronics engineering from NIT Calicut in 2018 and completed his MBA from IIM Indore in 2020. Farhana had completed her BTech from MES College of Engineering in Kuttippuram, Kerala.Family members said Aslam had been taking medication and undergoing therapy for depression for around 18 months. They said neither he nor Farhana had discussed any problems that might have suggested they were going through a difficult period.Faisal said relatives suspected work pressure could have contributed to the tragedy, although they had no confirmation of what the couple had been experiencing.“We used to go on trips together, and I connected very well with my brother-in-law. We suspect that work pressure in the IT sector may have led to the incident. They never discussed anything that suggested they were suffering or going through something so bad. Work pressure is the only reason we suspect, but only God and the two of them knew what was happening,” he said.Another relative, Abdul Azeez, said the family believed the incident may have occurred around midnight on Wednesday. Farhana was due to celebrate her birthday that day.“Her parents have been left shattered. We just want to take their bodies home,” he said.Email prompted colleagues to contact landlordAfter Aslam’s email arrived around 7am on Wednesday, his colleagues contacted the landlord using the details provided. The landlord went to the apartment, found the couple dead and alerted the police.An emergency response vehicle reached the spot around 8am, followed by a larger police team. An officer said the flat’s door was not bolted.Police recovered three laptops, two mobile phones, a rope, the note, a diary, scissors and a pen drive from the apartment. The electronic devices were seized for forensic analysis. Police said the note contained no allegations against anyone.Both bodies were shifted to a mortuary and identified by family members on Friday. Autopsies were yet to be conducted.“The cause of death will be established only after the autopsy report. articles.title: Deva, composer whose music announced Rajinikanth's stardom, dies at 75 in Chennai
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Deva, the music director whose \"Superstar\" title-card music has announced every Rajinikanth film since 1992, including the latest, Jailer 2, died
articles.body: CHENNAI: Deva, the music director whose "Superstar" title-card music has announced every Rajinikanth film since 1992, including the latest, Jailer 2, died in Chennai on Saturday. He was 75.He complained of chest pain on Saturday morning and was taken to Surya Hospital. He died despite efforts to resuscitate him, doctors said.The godfather of Gaana, Deva was a music director, lyricist and singer who took the street music of Chennai into mainstream cinema. He wrote and sang many of his own gaana numbers and was a rage through the 1990s. The songs he made popular are now sung even at international film events.At a time when Ilaiyaraaja dominated Tamil cinema and AR Rahman was ushering in a musical revolution, Deva carved out his own identity by speaking the language of the common man. Rather than competing with the two musical stalwarts, he built his reputation on simple, catchy tunes, familiar rhythms and colloquial expressions that resonated with audiences.Affectionately known as Thenisai Thendral, he became one of the most sought-after composers of the 1990s.For Rajinikanth, he created the vibe for the star's introductory songs, including those in Annamalai and Baashha. The Baashha theme became synonymous with Rajinikanth's screen persona, while Naan Autokaaran became an anthem for autorickshaw drivers in this part of the country.Deva also demonstrated his versatility through his association with Kamal Haasan, composing for films such as Avvai Shanmugi, which showcased a different musical sensibility from the larger-than-life hero themes he created for Rajinikanth.Born Devanesan Chokkalingam on Nov 20, 1950, in Mylapore, he came to film music after working in television and stage shows. His early musical exposure included classical training under Dhanraj, Western musical studies and stage performances. He worked at Doordarshan's Podhigai channel and composed songs for the farming programme Vayalum Vaazhvum. While his brothers, Sabesh and Murali, were also in the music business, his son, Srikanth Deva, is a composer too.Deva made his debut in 1989 with Manasukketha Maharaasaa. Prashanth's Vaikasi Porandhaachu in 1990 gave him his big break, establishing his ability to deliver accessible and emotionally engaging music.His other hits included Aasai, Kaadhal Kottai, Naerukku Ner, Vaali, Avvai Shanmugi, Kushi and Panchathanthiram. He worked in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam, and his scores run to more than 400 films.Despite his success, Deva remained known for his humility and appreciation of fellow musicians. He spoke admiringly of Ilaiyaraaja and Rahman and welcomed the work of younger composers, maintaining a reputation for simplicity both in his music and in his personal demeanour.Members of the film industry posted messages in memory of Deva.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: Can Yemen’s government forces sustain their offensive against the Houthis?
articles.summary: Houthi missile strikes threaten key supply routes on Yemen’s Red Sea coast, intensifying pressure on government forces.
articles.body:
Sanaa, Yemen – A missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi group, also known as Ansar Allah, streaks across the sky over Sanaa at midday, leaving a trail of smoke behind it.

Its intended target is unclear. It could have been a site in Saudi Arabia or territory to the south and east held by Yemen’s internationally recognised government. For people in northern Yemen, missile launches have become a familiar sight.

On Thursday, at least five people were killed near the al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden after Houthi missile strikes. Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani was present at the palace at the time of the attack, but was unharmed.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the attack targeted an operational headquarters, part of its campaign against Saudi-backed fighters and equipment supporting the internationally recognised government in Aden.

Frequent Houthi missile attacks – combined with the Iranian-backed group’s territorial gains around the city of Taiz in southwestern Yemen – have severed key supply routes and threatened other roads, ports, and airports that government forces rely on for supplies.

The disruptions could undermine the government’s Dawn of Yemen o peration , which aims to recapture territory held by the Houthi group. This includes the capital, Sanaa, which the Houthis seized at the start of the war in 2014.

Government officials, however, say supply issues will not halt the offensive, emphasising that their forces can overcome logistical challenges.

“The Houthi group consistently attempts to sever supply lines to government forces, but they have been unable to halt these supplies. So, military operations against the Houthis will continue,” Colonel Wadah al-Dubaish, spokesperson for the government-aligned Joint Forces on Yemen’s West Coast, told Al Jazeera.

But losses to the Houthis over the past few months have been damaging to the government.

A rapid Houthi advance south along the Red Sea coast in early September captured Mocha , a port on the Red Sea coast and a key supply hub for pro-government forces in western Taiz governorate.

A government counter-offensive reclaimed some of the territory lost in the southern Red Sea coast region, but not Mocha itself, which continues to be in Houthi hands.

Houthi attacks and ground advances, al-Dubaish said, may delay the delivery of supplies to government military forces or increase the cost of delivering supplies to certain fronts.

“However, they cannot stop the flow of supplies because the air, land and sea routes are still available, allowing supplies to continue reaching the front lines,” he said.

But the situation in the city of Taiz illustrates the limits of that logistical flexibility. Houthi forces have cut the main road connecting the city to Aden, the seat of the internationally recognised government. Alternative routes through the surrounding mountains have also been disrupted, leaving Taiz effectively besieged.

The consequences are already being felt. Fuel shortages and soaring prices have affected Taiz since the latest Houthi advances, with the cost of petrol tripling last week.

The loss of vital supply routes also threatens the government’s ability to deliver ammunition, reinforcements and other essential supplies to its troops, even as they face heavy and sustained Houthi attacks.

Al-Dubaish argued, however, that there are always advances and retreats in war, and that losing one battle does not mean losing the conflict as a whole.

“The war is still ongoing and will not cease until the Houthis are defeated,” he said.

Yemeni government forces are currently fighting the Houthis on several fronts in Yemen, including the southern Red Sea coast, around Taiz city, and in Marib and al-Jawf east of Sanaa.

Faisal al-Majidi, Yemen’s deputy minister of justice, told Al Jazeera that government forces rely on “logistical flexibility and decentralisation” to secure supply lines across the country.

“This approach involves dividing supply routes into semi-autonomous sectors, supported by nearby access points and key supply hubs – such as Shabwa, Marib, Houthi-free areas in Taiz, the Red Sea coast, and the southern governorates,” al-Majidi said.

Such an approach, he noted, mitigates the difficulties of moving between widely separated front lines.

“Furthermore, government forces have been fighting for the control of high points overlooking major roads to help protect vital supply arteries from bombardment,” al-Majidi added.

Among the areas pro-government forces have focused on is the strategic mountainous district of al-Waziiya in Taiz governorate, which overlooks the Red Sea coast and could also be a launching pad to relieve the siege on Taiz city from its western approaches. Fighting with the Houthis in al-Waziiya continues.

Saudi Arabia has stepped up its support for the Yemeni government and allied forces since the launch of Dawn of Yemen, acknowledging airstrikes against Houthi forces in the country for the first time since a 2022 truce. Riyadh first intervened in the conflict in Yemen in 2015 in an effort to restore the Yemeni government to Sanaa.

Al-Dubaish said the Saudi military role is a pivotal and indispensable source of support for Yemeni government forces.

“Saudi support is a decisive factor in the conflict. Without Saudi Arabia, it would be a huge challenge for the Yemeni government to confront the Houthis, who possess advanced military capabilities – such as ballistic and cruise missiles supplied by Iran – along with a large pool of fighters,” said al-Dubaish.

The Saudi-led coalition has said airstrikes have destroyed hundreds of high-value targets since early October.

Al-Majidi described the Saudi air support as a “strategic balancer” and a vital pillar of the Dawn of Yemen operation.

“The Saudi role centres on providing direct cover for ground forces and, more importantly, neutralising the reinforcements of the [Houthis], as well as targeting missile and drone launch platforms – thereby mitigating their destructive impact,” he said.

The Saudi-led coalition has previously airdropped weapons and ammunition to pro-government fighters in Taiz when it was besieged in the early years of the war, but there have been no reports of similar operations since the latest siege began this month.

Saudi Arabia is also vital for what may be an even more important task: uniting an anti-Houthi side that remains divided with disjointed command structures.

Al-Dubaish said that poor coordination among military units remains a significant challenge.

“The coordination problem stems from the presence of multiple military units operating under different command structures,” he added. “This fragmentation is not in the best interest of the forces fighting the Houthis.”

The government’s loss of the Red Sea coast in September was partly the result of faulty coordination among anti-Houthi forces, who appeared unable to respond quickly to the Houthi advance .

That was despite messaging from the Yemeni government since the start of the year that anti-Houthi forces were operating under a unified command structure, after the defeat of separatist Southern Transitional Council forces – who had been backed by the United Arab Emirates – at the start of the year.

“The coordination among various field forces … remains the true litmus test for the success of the Dawn of Yemen operation,” said al-Majidi.

Adnan al-Jabarni, a Yemeni researcher specialising in military affairs, told Al Jazeera that the level of coordination among government forces is improving.

“These forces are currently testing their coordination, given that they only began to operate under a unified structure – following the withdrawal of the UAE from Yemen and the formation of the Supreme Military Committee (SMC), which incorporated all the various branches and units,” al-Jabarni said.

In January, the Presidential Leadership Council, Yemen’s United Nations-recognised authority led by President Rashad al-Alimi, established the SMC , with the goal of overseeing all anti-Houthi military units and integrating them into the official Yemeni military under one command.

However, establishing the committee has not eliminated longstanding divisions between the different forces. Their command structures and sources of funding have historically differed, and the losses on the Red Sea coast have highlighted the continuing difficulties of coordinating their battlefield operations.

That coordination is vital for Taiz, where holding off the Houthis will depend on recapturing roads for use as supply routes.

Al-Jabarni argued that friction among pro-government forces is diminishing and the supply lines for government forces remain intact despite the Houthi attacks.

“The Houthis are attempting to exert pressure on Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government by targeting civilian facilities and supply lines – specifically focusing on vital infrastructure – but I believe this is likely to intensify the pace of anti-Houthi operations rather than slowing them down,” al-Jabarni said.

articles.title: He spent years in and out of prison - how a single book helped change everything
articles.summary: Omar Mentesh features in a new BBC documentary about the books which changed five people's lives.
articles.body:
"A book club in prison is the best thing on planet Earth, it really is," says Omar Mentesh, who spent nearly two decades in and out of jail from his teenage years.

"It's just people sharing, from all walks of life... and when they're in the book club, they find the book actually leads the conversation into other things. And I think for people who struggle to open up it was great."

The 44-year-old, from South Woodford in east London, features in a new BBC documentary led by Queen Camilla , called The Book That Changed My Life, which looks at how reading had a profound impact on five different people.

For Mentesh, what began as a means of escape became something that would change him forever.

Mentesh grew up on the Maiden Lane Estate in Camden.

"If you're going to be a kid, it's a perfect estate because there's a cubbyhole, alleyways, garages and places to run around. And unfortunately, places a kid shouldn't go," he tells BBC London.

One day, aged five, he and a group of friends went exploring through a hole in the fence by the estate's playground, which led to a train track.

"I remember taking a step forward and just feeling like someone was picking me up and was shaking me - and obviously I was being electrocuted.

"My shoes are the thing that saved my life, because they had rubber soles... but then the electricity had to exit somewhere and it exited through my head."

He woke up in hospital and while he says he doesn't remember feeling pain, he required plastic surgery "as my hands were melted", and suffered speech problems.

The accident meant he had to attend his early school years with bags over his injured hands and "I just couldn't write, it just felt like everyone else is cracking on and I just can't do it".

Feeling ostracised as he fell behind his classmates, Mentesh began breaking out of his primary school and before long his education became a distant past.

At the same time his parents' relationship broke down meaning his older brothers were left to help support the family and so "they just started committing crime, they was bunking off school, and I saw them doing it, and I just mimicked".

"I remember breaking into cars early... it's like they're legends and I was trying to copy it," he explains.

By the age of 15 Mentesh had received his first prison sentence.

But it was while locked up alone in Feltham Young Offender Institution that he first learned what reading could do as he found a copy of Jack Higgins's 1970s novel, The Eagle Has Landed, lying in his cell.

"It could have been any book, but I think that book there, the cover, it just enticed me," he says.

In that moment the World War Two spy thriller provided a means to escape his surroundings, but Mentesh later realised it was doing so much more.

"I probably read about half of it, understood about a quarter of it, but even just understanding a quarter of the book, that opened up the world for me.

"And it's not like I had an epiphany... It was just 'I appreciate reading' and then that there was enough because once you appreciate reading, the path is set, the foundations are set, and as long as you keep reading, change can only come."

Even so, Mentesh was still ingrained in organised crime and once released he was soon back to a life where "it was steal this and bring it to him, he'll give us money".

He says he lived by a "code in that you don't have to cause harm or commit violence to make money" as he began stealing printing and broadcast equipment to order.

Further prison sentences followed but each one would return him to his reading.

"I had to wait for that merry-go-round to go again, to read, develop my personality, my strengths, my values. And then every time I would go, I'd build up, I'd be growing as a person," he says.

However, it was his final crime that would have the most profound effect.

It was again intended to be a commercial burglary, this time at a jewellery store, but an error meant for the first time during one of his burglaries "there was a victim in the shop".

Mentesh doesn't elaborate on what happened other than saying that it "didn't sit well" and he will "forever apologise and regret what I did".

Jailed for seven years, reduced to five-and-a-half years on appeal, and with his personal life having "fallen apart", Mentesh faced "the perfect vacuum for books to fill that void".

"I had enough time to really build my education up where it needed to be to catch up what I lost when I was young," he explains.

At the same time he took on a role representing black, minority and ethnic prisoners, building on a job he did during another sentence in 2006.

"I learned a lot in that role, finding the skills I have in leading people who are in the wrong way in a hostile environment. And there's nothing more hostile than being a BME (black, minority and ethnic representative) in Exeter Prison," he says.

Released for the final time in 2017 and at that point in his 30s and homeless, Mentesh found himself sleeping on his sister's sofa before he moved to a hostel.

He then met his now-wife and after finding out she was pregnant "that was it, and I said, 'what do I do from here?'".

Building on the education he had gained while in jail, he first went to college for two years before attending Queen Mary University where he gained a degree in business management.

Job placements followed, as well as work with charities, before he set up Anabranch, a company which works to rehabilitate prisoners.

Mentesh says the firm's name, taken from the part of a river that splits off before reconnecting with the main waterway further downstream, is apt to his own story.

"I was part of society for a little bit and then I was removed from it, and then I was put back further downstream," he says.

Along with this work, he remains a keen book advocate, working with charities to support literacy programmes, as well as still being a prolific reader.

The next book on his reading list is Previous Engagements by Bruce Shand, the Queen's father. She gave it to him following the BBC documentary.

The book examines how Shand came to love books while a prisoner of war during World War Two, something Mentesh relates to from his discovery of The Eagle Has Landed in his first prison cell.

"For me, books meant a whole lot more than just passing time," he says.

"I thought I was just getting knowledge... I didn't know a book actually has the power to change a person."
